text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"multiple paragraph structure with intro, body, and conclusion","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is arranged into clear sections that make the argument easier to follow from claim to wrap-up."},{"evidence":"“Why would a consumer buy a ‘driverless’ car when they still have to remain alert?”","quality":"rhetorical development","description":"The essay uses pointed rhetorical questions and explanation to press its position and extend its reasoning."},{"evidence":"“The whole issue is messy and definitely not practical” after discussing laws and liability","quality":"argument coherence","description":"The essay keeps its reasons tied to one central claim that driverless cars are impractical."},{"evidence":"direct references to Google, BMW, traffic laws, and liability","quality":"use of textual evidence","description":"The essay supports its stance with multiple relevant details from the source article rather than general assertions."},{"evidence":"“however,” “Even if,” “For the most part,” “ultimately”","quality":"transitional control","description":"The essay uses clearer transitions to connect ideas and signal shifts in the argument."}]}
